sources.go: GO/h{1,2}.custom.GO (lab-built, both haplotypes, with term names)
sources.pfam_panther: annotation_info.txt for HAP1; parsed from defline.txt for HAP2 because HAP2's annotation_info domain columns are empty in the release

chromatin.accessible_region_definition: genic or within 2 kb of the start, replicates merged -- the source paper's own classification. A 500 bp window fails, because 55% of conserved gene starts have their nearest accessible region more than 2 kb away, which is that paper's headline finding about distal elements in plants.
chromatin.scope: A property OF THE P. TRICHOCARPA ORTHOLOG, not of the 717 gene. No chromatin data exists for 717 or for either parent species. Attached only where the ortholog call is reciprocal 1:1.
chromatin.source: GEO GSE128434 (Lu, Marand, Schmitz et al., Nature Plants 2019), P. trichocarpa leaf: ATAC-seq, H3K4me3, H3K36me3, and matched RNA-seq
chromatin.the_standing_limit: ATAC and H3K4me3 establish THAT a locus has a promoter, never WHERE transcription starts. Only a 5'-end method does that, and none exists for any Populus.
chromatin.why_expression_gates_it: The chromatin is leaf only. A gene silent in leaf correctly carries no promoter mark there, so an absent mark says nothing about the gene unless you know it was expressed. The source analysis's first run failed its own gate for exactly this reason.

corrections.what: expression tissue baseline + tau regrouped by tissue_analysis, not tissue
corrections.why: tissue pooled leaf_young + leaf_old (46 samples, all study 1) into one 'leaf' bucket; the WT-control subset of that pool was 11 + 11 of 77

cre.dropped_family_lfy: identically zero genome-wide (n_matrices=1, length-biased threshold), see build_cre.py docstring
cre.hit_definition: log-odds PSSM (pseudocount 0.5, log2 vs a uniform 0.25 background), scanned on both strands; a position is a hit when its score is at least HIT_FRAC of that motif's own maximum attainable score
cre.not_included: per-matrix enrichment statistics and LSG-vs-control comparisons; those are population-level chapter results, not per-gene facts

positions.families: the nine named TF families only; `other` (457 matrices) is excluded as not meaningful to draw per-motif
positions.gate: every shipped gene's positions aggregate exactly to its cre.fam counts, asserted on every build
positions.measure: bp from the transcription start to the motif's 5' (far) edge, within the 1 kb promoter window
positions.why_some_are_withheld: Upstream scanned a 3 kb window and took the 1 kb slice, with a greedy non-overlapping pass global over 3 kb. Only the 1 kb FASTA is on this cluster, so a motif near the boundary can be resolved differently: 45 of 63,960 genes disagree on a named family, all in the direction of this scan finding MORE hits. Those genes are withheld rather than shown with positions that contradict published counts.

crossspecies.note: Only reciprocal 1:1 pairs are presented as orthologs. Ambiguous ones keep their multiplicity rather than being resolved by taking a top hit.
crossspecies.source: this atlas's own GENESPACE run 47798208, syntenicHits

duplication.scope: Chapter tier-2 selection, NOT genome-wide: pairs are concentrated at phylostrata 16-18 with a rank-12 Pentapetalae comparator set. Any Ks distribution here describes that selection, not the genome.
duplication.source: master_duplication_table_v9.csv (rule 5c + 178-conflict WGD resolution, TD union set) -- supersedes dupclass_membership_v8.csv

kaks.ps19: 1 of 681 PS19 genes has any trichocarpa pair. A structural absence, not missing data -- a hybrid-only gene has no ortholog to measure against.
kaks.reading: Monotone with youth and well below the neutral 1. Young genes are constrained, just less constrained -- not neutrally evolving, which is what a spurious open reading frame would look like.
kaks.selection_bias: Pairing rate falls with youth (87.6% ancient, 39.1% PS18, ~0% PS19), so the young-gene omega is measured on the conserved end of its stratum and if anything understates the relaxation.
kaks.why_not_yn00: NG86 and YN00 omega correlate at r = 0.07 to 0.36 PER GENE on these alignments while their class medians agree to within 0.06 -- median dS is about 0.04, too close for YN00 to be stable gene by gene. NG86 is the one with external support: r = 0.937 against the atlas's independently derived allele omega, against YN00's 0.083. yn00_omega ships only to show the spread, never as a per-gene answer.

layers.esmfold_note: ESMFold structure covers 40,685 of 63,960 genes (64%). Absence is coverage, not a structural claim.
layers.proteomics_note: Three independent PXD datasets, reported separately. Detection rates differ ~4x (3,989 / 18,739 / 21,449 genes), so a gene absent from one is not undetected.

lsg_pool.not_licensed: The corrected pool is not evidence that the surviving calls are modelled-safe. abSENSE corrects detection FAILURE (sensitivity); a missing genome is taxon SAMPLING (coverage). 86% of the genes Idesia removed were `no_prediction` in the frozen abSENSE run.
lsg_pool.note: PS18 and PS19 are never pooled. 179 genes moved PS19 -> PS18 and stayed in the pool; none moved the other way. Numbers published against the frozen pool are correct statements about that pool and are not retracted -- they must name it.
lsg_pool.tax_rep_note: tax_rep is the fraction of the panel's genomes represented in the gene's stratum, so it moves for genes whose RANK did not: the denominator went from 12 genomes to 13. Not a re-call, a re-scaling.

at_the_boundary_species.direction: abSENSE OVER-predicts what a Salix homolog would have scored. An expected score that is too high makes an observed absence look more surprising than it is, which under-estimates detection_failure_prob and over-calls surprising_absence.
at_the_boundary_species.species: Salix purpurea -- the rank-18 boundary. Every HDF flag on this pool is a prediction at this species.

absense_calibration.headline: abSENSE flags are worst calibrated at exactly the boundary that defines this pool, and biased in the direction that over-calls a young gene. Quote the flag with this number, never alone.
absense_calibration.measured: 2026-09-09, abSENSE --predall over 868,127 predicted-vs-observed bitscore pairs (ms2-lsg analyses/absense_hdf, jobs 48015768_1/_2)
absense_calibration.not_retracted: Nothing in the QC layer is withdrawn by this, and the pool correction does not rest on abSENSE at all -- 776/835 comes from genEra ranks with Idesia added. What is qualified is the per-gene HDF flag and any statement resting on it.
absense_calibration.this_is_the_optimistic_bound: It is measured in-sample, and on the wrong genes: a Salix pair only exists for a gene that HAS a Salix homolog, which by definition is not an LSG. For a real PS18 gene the Salix prediction is pure out-of-sample extrapolation. 0.59-0.61 is what the model achieves at that boundary on the easy cases.

flags_on_the_withdrawn_pool.note: the same five counts over all 1,725 source rows, i.e. against the frozen pool these flags were cut for. Kept so numbers already published against that pool stay checkable.

lsg_qc.note: flags, not filters -- nothing here removes, renumbers or filters a gene, and the atlas must not use these fields to shrink the pool count. The pool size is set by data/meta manifest.lsg_pool, never by these flags.
lsg_qc.source_pool: This file was cut against the WITHDRAWN frozen pool (1,725 rows). Rows for genes the Idesia-corrected panel took out of the pool are dropped here, per the source's own scope rule that a non-pool gene has no young-age claim to qualify. The withdrawn call stays visible on those genes under ps.frz.

phylostrat.note: LSG pool = rank >= 18 (PS18 Populus + PS19 hybrid-only), per the chapter definition. PS17 Saliceae is flanking context and is not in the pool. Ranks are the Idesia-corrected 13-genome panel adopted 2026-09-09; the withdrawn 12-genome call is kept per gene under ps.frz wherever the two disagree.

proteomics.cross_species_caveat: Three of the five datasets are other Populus species, whose samples contain no 717 protein. A hit there says the gene FAMILY is translated somewhere in Populus, not that 717's copy is.
proteomics.detectability_note: `abl` says whether the gene has any fully-tryptic peptide in the searchable window. Read it before reading a zero: a protein with none is invisible however abundant it is, and that is a composition property on which young genes differ.
proteomics.engine_caveat: A Sage 1% FDR is not an MSFragger 1% FDR. Report the engine with the number.
proteomics.method: raw-spectra re-search against a database CONTAINING the 717 proteins (98,659 targets), Sage 0.14.7, 1% peptide AND spectrum FDR

how_indirect_it_usually_is.measured_on: PXD025636, the deepest of the five datasets
how_indirect_it_usually_is.reading: For most genes the assignment rests on a peptide that is neither species-specific nor gene-specific. That does not make the protein absent; it makes 'this gene's product was observed' the wrong reading of it. The card now shows which kind of evidence each gene has.

peptide_detail.per_gene_per_dataset: n peptides, n PSMs, best hyperscore, how many peptides are unique to this gene, how many are absent from the P. trichocarpa proteome, and up to 3 example peptides
peptide_detail.why: 'detected in N of 5 datasets' hid the difference between a peptide unique to this gene and absent from every other species, and a peptide shared with P. trichocarpa and with dozens of other 717 genes. Those are different claims.

proteomics.supersedes: Tier-1 string matching against three third-party peptide tables built from another species' database (PXD023826 / PXD025636 / PXD064017). A Tier-1 negative was uninformative by construction. PXD023826 and PXD064017 are not covered by this layer -- the replacement is deeper and interpretable, not a strict superset of datasets.
proteomics.union_fdr_caveat: 1% per dataset ACCUMULATES over five datasets. Read a single-dataset singleton against the pooled false-peptide expectation, not one dataset's.

excluded.PtXaTreH.08G115400: ESMFold PDB is 0 bytes; also absent from the SS table

structure.gate: per-residue arrays reproduce n_residues, mean_plddt, frac_plddt_lt70, helix_frac and strand_frac of secondary_structure_summary.tsv to half a unit of its last decimal, for every gene; and every shard ss value is that table rounded to 3 decimals
structure.what: ESMFold Calpha trace (0.1 A), per-residue pLDDT, sequence and pydssp c3 secondary structure. Not the full-atom model: that is 2.3 GB gzipped, over the Pages site cap.
